title: iOS 27: What’s new, what’s in the latest beta and what’s coming next
content:
Macworld





Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. But more features are on the way, and the latest beta offers a preview of what’s coming next.
iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier.
iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.
This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible iPhones and the latest beta developments. We also explain what’s expected in the next update, when it could arrive and which features are still to come.


What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.


						

							


iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.0.1
The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixes unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously.
iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple has confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.
Apple says affected iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T should install iOS 27.0.1 along with a new carrier settings update, which together are intended to prevent the problem. The carrier update should install automatically within 14 days, or users can check for it by going to Settings > General > About. However, the updates cannot repair phones that have already been affected: Apple says devices that have lost service because of the issue cannot be reactivated through software and will need to be replaced through Apple or AT&T.
The iPhone Duo will ship with iOS 27.1. Apple has not confirmed whether other iPhones will receive that version; iOS 27.2 is currently in beta. The iPhone Duo is due to go on sale on October 23.
After that, iOS 27.2 is expected to be the next major update and is currently in beta.


						

							


iOS 27 beta – What’s coming next?
Latest beta: iOS 27.2 
It seems that Apple will only use iOS 27.1 number for the iPhone Duo’s release.
The iOS 27.2 beta 1 was released on September 16, followed by 27.2 beta 2 on September 21. The public beta of iOS 27.2 arrived on September 22. Developer beta 3, was released October 5.
When iOS 27.2 arrives it is expected to introduce the following:
Redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights.
Bug fixes and performance improvements addressing issues in iOS 27.
Additional Siri AI languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
Suggested replies in Messages, previously removed before iOS 27 launched.
Automatic password changes for compromised passwords.


						

							


What features are still to come in iOS 27
At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Missing features include: 
Redesigned Health app: A completely redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights is coming later in 2026.
Additional Siri AI languages: Siri AI launched in English only. French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish are due in October. 
Smarter suggested replies in Messages: Suggested replies that better reflect the user’s writing style appeared during beta testing but were removed before the public release. 
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 
SynthID identification for AI images: Apple said support for adding SynthID identification to most AI-generated or edited images would arrive in a software update later in 2026. 


						

							


What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.
Siri AI features
More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customization requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.
If you haven’t got Siri AI yet find out how here: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?
Read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages.
How good is Siri AI?
Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.
Even in our early tests during the beta, Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful. 
It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.
Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.
However, Siri AI is launching as a “beta” feature and still requires a bit of polish. It’s also only available in English at first, with a handful of other languages/regions, arriving in a later update.
Regional Siri AI availability
Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. The first release only supports the English language, and initially has Expressive Voices for English (UK) and English (US). Several other languages are coming with the iOS 27.1 update in October.
Siri AI compatibility
Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro or the new iPhone 18 Pro. 


						

							


Apple Intelligence across apps
As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari can organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos gains a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar can now understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.


						

							


New features coming to apps in iOS 27
iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the iPhone Duo.
Safari
Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.
There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Photos
Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.
Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.
Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.
Camera
iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manual focus along with Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.
The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.
Messages

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Messages gets several useful improvements.
You can decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.
Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note, or finding relevant photos.
Messages in iOS 27 will gains smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. (This was removed from the iOS 27 beta and wasn’t available at the launch of iOS 27).
Drawing

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.
Mail
Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.
Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.
Phone
A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.
Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.
FaceTime
FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call.
Passwords

				
					

				
			
Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple




The Passwords app continues to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 will go a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically.
Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.
The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.
Apple removed this ability to detect compromised passwords and replace them from the beta shortly before the release of iOS 27. It’s expected to arrive with a later update. 
Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.
Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.
Calendar
Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.
Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.
Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.
Image Playground
Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.
Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.
AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content. This particular feature wasn’t available at launch, but Apple has confirmed it is coming later. 
Wallet
Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.
Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.
Weather
Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.
Home app
Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.
Maps
Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.
Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.
Podcasts
Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.
Fitness
Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.
Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.


						

							


iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone 
CarPlay
CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.
AirPods
iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.
A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.
Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.
Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.
Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.


						

							


Other changes in iOS 27
It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.
Home Screen and landscape mode
Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.
These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.
iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.
Liquid Glass refinements

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.
Ringtones, alarms and alert volume
iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.
Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:
Ringtones
Alarms and timers
Alerts and system sounds
The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.
Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.
Keyboard
iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.
It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.
Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.
Privacy and Find My
iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.
Recovery and troubleshooting
Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.


						

							


System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster
Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.
Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.
The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.
Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.
More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.
That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.


						

							


Child safety and parental controls

				
					

				
			
Apple




There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.
This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.
Ask to Browse: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.
Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.
Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.
Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.
Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. 
Problems with Parental Control set up 
Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.
Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.
To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.
Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.


						

							


Accessibility changes in iOS 27
Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:
VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.


						

							


iOS 27 compatibility 

				
					

				
			iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.
Roman Loyola/IDG




According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.
Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.
There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.
However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.
The iOS 27 compatibility list is:
iPhone 17e (launched in 2026) 
iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)
iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022)
iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022)
iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)
iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020)
iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)
The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When was iOS 27 released?
iOS 27 was released on September 14, 2026.





2.
Which iPhones get iOS 27?
The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features require iPhone 15 Pro or newer, and the new more expressive Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, or newer.





3.
Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?
The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have a standard iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

Sometimes, efforts to recreate famous old computer systems involve the use of more modern parts. In the case of one exhibit from the Museo de Historia de la Computacion in Spain, it's a visual replica of the Cray-1 supercomputer, but with it relying on the power of out-of-date Mac minis.
The replica, first reported by Ars-Technica is both a celebration of the 50th anniversary of the Cray-1, as well as that of Apple's founding. Matching the styling of the original Cray-1, it's a tower of vertically-mounted Mac minis behind green and clear glass.

title: AirPods 5 vs. AirPods 5 With Wireless Charging Case Buyer's Guide
content:
Apple offers two versions of the AirPods 5: a $129 model with a USB-C Charging Case and a $149 model with a Wireless Charging Case. The extra $20 also buys longer battery life, swipe volume controls, and additional Find My features, so there are differences between the earbuds themselves as well as their cases.


Both models include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, the H2 chip, the same open-ear design, and the same redesigned acoustic architecture with updated Adaptive EQ. They also share Transparency mode, Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Spatial Audio, Voice Isolation, studio-quality audio recording, and IP57 dust, sweat, and water resistance. Both support Live Translation when paired with a compatible iPhone with Apple Intelligence enabled, in supported languages and regions.

The earbuds have identical dimensions and weight. The cases are also the same size, although the Wireless Charging Case is slightly heavier. There are still some notable differences to justify the price difference. Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these sets of AirPods is best for you.



AirPods 5
AirPods 5 With Wireless Charging Case


Force sensor
Force sensor with swipe volume controls


Up to four hours of listening time on a single charge with Active Noise Cancellation enabled (up to six hours with noise control off)
Up to five hours of listening time on a single charge with Active Noise Cancellation enabled (up to seven hours with noise control off)


Up to 20 hours of listening time with the charging case with Active Noise Cancellation enabled
Up to 22 hours of listening time with the charging case with Active Noise Cancellation enabled


Charging Case (USB-C)
Wireless Charging Case (USB-C) with support for the Apple Watch charger and Qi-certified chargers



Case speaker for Find My and charging and battery status sounds


Find My with last-connected location and sound playback on the earbuds
Find My network tracking, sound playback on the earbuds, separate locations for each earbud and the case, and individual Lost Mode support


Charging case weighs 32.3 grams (1.14 ounces)
Charging case weighs 34.7 grams (1.22 ounces)


$129
$149




For most people, the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case are clearly the better buy. The extra $20 is a very small premium for conveniences you are likely to appreciate if you use your AirPods regularly. Longer listening time is useful for travel and extended sessions, while swipe volume controls let you make adjustments without reaching for your iPhone or asking Siri.

The higher-end model is worth considering even if you plan to charge exclusively over USB-C. Wireless charging becomes more useful if you already have a Qi charger or Apple Watch charger. Its additional Find My features are valuable if you tend to misplace your AirPods, allowing you to locate the earbuds and case separately and use the Find My network when they are beyond your device's range. The case speaker also helps when it slips between cushions or gets buried in a bag.

The standard AirPods 5 make more sense if you are on a very strict budget, want a secondary pair, or mostly listen for short periods. You still get the same audio technology and noise cancellation, so saving $20 does not mean compromising on those core features. You simply need to be comfortable with USB-C charging, shorter battery life, fewer controls, and more limited Find My functionality.

are not interchangeable between the two models. If you buy the standard AirPods 5, you cannot add wireless charging later by purchasing the other model's case, making it worth deciding which features you want before buying.

title: Top Stories: Apple's 'Welcome Home' Launch on October 13 and More
content:
Following the usual September rush of Apple news, it looks like October is also about ready to explode, with not just one but two rounds of Apple product debuts this month sandwiched around the iPhone Duo launch.


A first launch on October 13 has been confirmed by Apple and will clearly be focused on the home as has been rumored, while it appears a second round a couple of weeks later will focus on new Macs and perhaps a few more things still in Apple's pipeline, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more!

Top Stories

Apple Product Launch Announced for October 13: 'Welcome Home'

Apple has announced an upcoming product launch that will take place on Tuesday, October 13. It looks like it will arrive as a batch of press releases, with select members of the media getting hands-on time with the new products at an "Apple Experience" in New York City at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time that day.


We are expecting Apple's announcement to focus on new smart home products, including the long-rumored smart home hub, a new Apple TV 4K, and a refreshed HomePod mini.

iPhone Duo pre-orders also begin next week, and even that might not be all for the month of October as MacRumors has heard there may be another set of product launches in the final week of the month and Bloomberg has corroborated the rumor. We're still expecting updates for several Mac models that would likely come in the final wave, as well as a new iPad mini.

Three Years of 80% Charge Limits on iPhone: The Results

Since 2023, Apple's newer iPhones have had an optional 80 percent charge limit for those who want to extend battery lifespan. Charging to 80 percent instead of 100 percent is supposed to put less stress on the battery, improving longevity.


For the last three years, MacRumors managing editor Juli Clover has used that setting on her iPhones, starting with the iPhone 15 Pro Max, then the iPhone 16 Pro Max, and most recently, the iPhone 17 Pro Max.

her iPhone 17 Pro Max is at 97 percent maximum capacity with a cycle count of 277, which is pretty good, but we want to know how that compares to other users who have used different charging strategies, so please share yours in the discussion thread!

Apple Says iPhone 18 Pro Max Users With AT&T Cellular Issue Need to Have Device Replaced

Since the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max last month, a number of U.S. customers with the Pro Max model on AT&T have run into issues with their devices losing cellular service and no way to fix the issue.


AT&T last week sent out text messages to iPhone 18 Pro Max users urging them to update "immediately" to iOS 27.0.1, which was released by Apple on September 28. While that update does not fix the service issues for affected users, it will apparently help keep the issue from impacting devices that have yet to run into problems.

affected devices have to be replaced. Notably, iPhone 18 Pro Max models sold in the United States are the only ones in the iPhone 18 Pro family to still use a Qualcomm cellular modem rather than Apple's own C2 modem, but it's unclear if that is related to the issue.

MacBook Pro With OLED Display Rumored to Be 'Significantly Lighter'

One of the Mac updates we're expecting to see as part of a reported October 27 launch is the long-rumored high-end MacBook with a touchscreen OLED display.


Notably, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says that these machines will be "significantly lighter" than the current MacBook Pro models, though they won't be much thinner.

new animation when long pressing on Dock icons that's similar to what's seen on touch-based operating systems like iOS and iPadOS, plus code for a number of new touch-specific gestures.

LG Making Doorbell, Lock, and Cameras for Apple's Home Hub

In a bit of an unusual development, Apple will be partnering with LG for its upcoming smart home push set to be unveiled on Tuesday, with the two companies working together on accessories that will be released under the LG brand rather than as Apple-branded products.


Products like doorbells, smart locks, and cameras will be included in the lineup, and regulatory documents and leaked code have already provided glimpses of some of the products. While the products are being released by LG, the collaboration with Apple will give them tighter integration and simpler setup within the Apple ecosystem.

Apple Announces 'Full Disk Access' Changes on macOS Due to AI Agents

In a post on its developer news website late last week, Apple announced that it will be introducing "additional controls" for the "Full Disk Access" setting on macOS due to new risks posed by AI agents. This comes amid the rise of always-on AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, which have prompted privacy concerns.


"Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users' full knowledge and understanding," said Apple.

"As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially," it added.

The holiday season has begun, and that means it’s time for traditions. Though the TV app on the iPhone, iPad, or Mac
On smart TVs with the Apple TV app
On the web at tv.apple.com

title: How to adjust the vibration on your Apple Watch
content:
Macworld





The Apple Watch can vibrate to let you now about a notification. But you might find that the vibration isn’t strong enough for you to notice. Or, you might want to disable vibrations completely.
Apple offers three vibration settings: Off, Standard, and Prominent. If you’ve bought an Apple Watch and never changed this setting, Standard is the default. There are two ways to adjust it: directly on your Apple Watch or in the Watch app on your paired iPhone.
To adjust the vibration on the Apple Watch, go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Haptics.
To adjust the Apple Watch vibration in the Watch app on your iPhone, open the Watch app and go to My Watch > Sounds & Haptics > Haptics.
Select the option you want from the list there. Off turns off vibration for notifications completely. Standard makes the Apple Watch vibrate twice. Distinctive makes it vibrate once for a long time and then twice briefly.
This setting only adjusts the vibration for notifications. There are also two other, less noticeable types of vibration: that of the Digital Crown and system haptics. Both are simply used to provide feedback when operating the Apple Watch.
While the Digital Crown’s vibration is largely self-explanatory, system haptics generally serve to confirm various interactions with the Apple Watch. For example, when you use the double-tap and wrist gestures, the Apple Watch vibrates to confirm.
You cannot customize these two types of vibration; you can only switch them on or off. They can be found under Settings > Sounds & Haptics or My Watch > Sounds & Haptics in the System Sounds & Haptics section at the bottom of the list. To disable the Digital Crown vibration, toggle the switch under Haptics (Crown); to disable system haptics, toggle the switch under System Haptics.

title: SpaceX Inches Closer to Becoming a U.S. Carrier
content:
SpaceX this week announced two developments that further its goal of becoming a major U.S. carrier to compete with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile.


It is acquiring a low-band spectrum license portfolio in the 800MHz band, which it says addresses one of the "remaining technical gaps" that will let it to compete with other carriers. Most smartphones already support the 800MHz band SpaceX is buying.

The FCC approved the Starlink Mobile Gen2 constellation application, letting SpaceX launch 15,000 satellites optimized for 2GHz spectrum globally. The company says the Starlink Mobile satellites will "deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth" of the current generation. The FCC also issued SpaceX a waiver permitting the company to offer wireless service through its satellites without a spectrum leasing agreement with a terrestrial carrier.

After receiving final FCC approval for the new spectrum purchase, SpaceX will combine its satellites with an "advanced terrestrial deployment" to connect devices everywhere. SpaceX says the 2GHz mid-band spectrum will offer high-bandwidth capacity in the U.S., while the new low-band spectrum will allow Starlink's signal to penetrate through obstacles like walls.

SpaceX plans to be the first network operator to deploy satellite and terrestrial spectrum. It says it will offer a single network with "a reliable service indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between."

title: Welcome Home: 4 big Apple announcements coming next week
content:
Macworld





October is shaping up to be an exceptionally busy month at Apple Park. Apple is readying the iPhone Duo, a revamped Health app in iOS 27.2, a touchscreen MacBook Pro, and an overhauled iPad mini, which are all expected to launch by the end of this month. But that won’t be all.
Apple announced on Thursday that it will be holding a special “Welcome Home” experience on October 13, where it will presumably launch its new smart home products. According to credible rumors, the devices will include next-generation Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini models, along with a brand-new home hub. While many enthusiasts may perceive some of next week’s Apple TV and HomePod upgrades as unexciting performance boosts, the chip bumps will actually unlock never-before-seen advantages for Apple’s smart home line.
An all-new platform
The star of the show will undoubtedly be the dedicated home hub—what some are referring to as the HomePad. Hardware-related leaks and OS code references already give us a solid idea of what to expect from this forthcoming device, including its approximate size and some of its software perks.
The HomePad will offer a 6-inch, square-shaped touchscreen stitched to a HomePod-like speaker and draw AC power. Users will be able to display memories from their photo libraries when it’s idle—presumably depending on who’s detected nearby. It will rely on the built-in camera to recognize household members and surface apps/data accordingly, in addition to providing for FaceTime video calls.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s new smart platform is expected to use elements of the iPhone’s Standby mode when not in use.

Apple




Perhaps the most exciting aspect of the HomePad is the all-new homeOS, which will certainly introduce its own unique user interface and feature set to justify the creation of such a device. Apple TV 4K and HomePod models already act as HomeKit hubs, and the iPad is perfectly capable of controlling smart home accessories. So, it’s safe to assume that the HomePad will bring new features, enticing customers to add it to their existing setups.
Smarter speaker
The HomePod mini has been around for six years, providing a decent listening experience, seamless Apple ecosystem integrations, and basic voice command support in a miniature design. During the October 13 launch, Apple could finally unveil the HomePod mini 2, bringing fresh color options, potential audio improvements, and a faster S-series chip. While this may sound like an iterative upgrade, the HomePod mini 2 will finally resolve its predecessor’s main flaw.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Despite its smart speaker classification, the HomePod mini is currently powered by the classic Siri, which is anything but smart. The voice assistant frequently struggles to perform basic actions, requires precise phrasing, and instructs users to check their iPhones for complex answers. 
The HomePod mini 2 will address that by adopting Siri AI, allowing you to speak more naturally and get hands-free answers based on its trained data and your personal information. Many users will finally be satisfied with the HomePod’s overall performance, minimizing the need to hunt for smarter third-party alternatives like those from Google and Amazon.
A19 TV perks
Similar to the HomePod mini, the imminent Apple TV 4K 4’s most prominent highlight will be the introduction of a faster chip. First released in 2022, the current model packs the iPhone 13’s A15 Bionic chipset with 4GB of RAM. Next week’s model could bump that to an A19 or A19 Pro SoC from last year’s iPhone 17 lineup, increasing the RAM to 8GB or 12GB. This will bring Siri AI to the big screen and enhance the set-top box’s general performance. That seems unlikely to be the full story.
Opting for a year-old flagship smartphone processor in the midst of a chip shortage crisis solely for Siri AI support does not add up—especially since TVs aren’t primary AI consumption devices. Had it been the case, Apple could’ve easily repurposed the iPhone 15 Pro’s A17 Pro chip and gotten away with it.

				
					

				
			Apple wants you to game on your Apple TV, and a much better processor could help.
Foundry




As such, I presume the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K will bring meaningful software additions that take full advantage of the A19, like a more serious gaming push. Given that Beats has allegedly been developing game controllers, this theory could realistically materialize. Otherwise, no one is paying over two hundred bucks to stream Netflix and chill with Siri AI in the living room.
The great unknown
While iPhone hardware components tend to leak in advance all the time, Apple has a tighter grip over its software development teams. During pretty much every press event, the company surprises us with fresh OS features introductions that had been built in utter secrecy. These features often roll out to older devices, too, despite being marketed for the latest and greatest releases.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




So even if you’re not planning to upgrade your current Apple smart home devices, the next software update could still elevate your experience with significant additions—like iOS 27.2’s four-HomePod surround sound setup.

Mac mini
A vinyl skin makes the most sense for anyone who wants to change the Mac mini's appearance while preserving its compact footprint. Unlike a case, a skin provides cosmetic protection rather than meaningful protection against drops.
The 2026 Mac mini keeps the same dimensions as the enclosure Apple introduced with the M4 generation, measuring 5 inches square and 2 inches tall. The shared dimensions keep many M4-era skin designs relevant to the newer Mac mini.
XtremeSkins already sells a product specifically labeled for the M6 Mac mini, while Slickwraps, ArmorSuit, and Capes continue to list their skins for the 2024 model. The biggest differences come down to design, material, coverage, and price.

title: DarkSword and Coruna iOS exploits continue to attack crypto wallets
content:
Macworld





A new report by security researchers at Censys warns that the DarkSword exploit on iOS continues to be used in conjunction with Coruna malware to steal cryptocurrency wallets. Discovered earlier this year, DarkSword/Coruna is a dual-edged hacking toolkit. DarkSword attacks WebKit and JavaScriptCore to access iOS’s SpringBoard that managing app launch and the Home screen. Coruna is the payload used to steal crypto wallet information.
Censys’ research found several servers that had DarkSword/Coruna deployment directories. Wallet apps being targeted include Bitpie, Coinbase, Exodus, imToken, MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Uniswap, and OKEx. According to the site’s researchers, the exploit’s main purpose is wallet theft and also “mines Photos and Notes for BIP39 recovery phrases.”
As we reported back in March, old versions of iOS are vulnerable to DarkSword. All of the security holes used by DarkSword have been fixed as of iOS 26.3 (the current version is iOS 27.0.1). Users of older versions of iOS 26, iOS 18, and earlier may be vulnerable.
How to protect your iPhone from malware
The easiest task to perform to secure your iPhone is to update the operating system. iOS can be updated in the Settings app by tapping General > Software Update. Apple also has a separate method for installing immediate security patches called Background Security Improvements. It is located in Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom to find Background Security Improvements. Macworld has a list of tips for keeping your iPhone secure.

title: Apple Arcade in October: Five new games added to the service
content:
Macworld





Gaming subscription services are all the rage now, but Apple Arcade isn’t a little different from the likes of PlayStation Plus, EA Play, or Xbox Game Pass. If you’ve got questions about it, we’ve got plenty of answers.
Updated October 9, 2026: There are five new games on the service this month: 4 Pics 1 Word+, Pusheen’s Place, River City Survivors, Terraria+, and Touchgrind BMX 2+.
What is Apple Arcade?
Apple Arcade is a gaming subscription service for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and AppleTV that features several hundred games. The games are a mix of genres and styles, and include original games you’ll only find on the service and others that can be found on the regular App Store or even other platforms. Apple Arcade isn’t a streaming service like Xbox Live Cloud Gaming or GeForce NOW. Games must be downloaded onto your device in order to be played.
What do I need to run it?
Apple Arcade was made available as part of iOS 13, iPad OS 13, tvOS 13, and macOS Catalina or later. Some of the more visually-intensive games may only run well on newer hardware, though, and some Mac games require macOS 11 (Big Sur).
How much does Apple Arcade cost?
Apple Arcade costs $6.99/£6.99 per month, and you’ll also get a one-month free trial or you can get three months free if you purchase a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV or Mac. To claim your free trial click here.
You can get Apple Arcade for less than $6.99 a month if you subscribe for a year upfront. A year of Apple Arcade is $49.99/£49.99 (so $4.16 a month). If you’re currently on the $6.99 month-to-month plan and want to switch to the annual plan and save some money, you can do so on your iPhone or iPad. Open the App Store app, then tap your account icon in the upper right. Tap Subscriptions, then tap the entry for Apple Arcade. Here, you can switch to the annual plan. 
Apple Arcade is also included in the Apple One subscription bundles, which range from $20 a month to $38 a month and include access to Apple Music and Apple TV and iCloud storage. There is also a month free trial of Apple One. To claim the trial, or sign up for Apple One, click here.
How do I sign up for Apple Arcade?
There isn’t an Apple Arcade app—it’s built into the App Store. On your iPhone, iPad, or Mac open the App Store and look for the Apple Arcade tab at the bottom of the screen (or in the left column on macOS). A sign-up screen with a Try It Free button will appear. After the trial you’ll be charged either the monthly or annual fee, depending on your selection. When subscribing, you’ll need to enter your Apple ID password or use Touch ID or Face ID to sign in, and you’ll have to confirm your subscription purchase a few times.

				
					

				
			
Once you’re done with the sign up, the Arcade section of the App Store shows what games are available to you. To access a game, tap on it in the App Store, then tap the Get button. When the game is done installing on your device, the Get button turns into a Play button, and you can tap it to launch the game. The game app icon will also appear on your device’s Home page.
On the Apple TV, there actually is an Arcade app. Open that to see the sign-up offer. You’ll also find an Arcade tab within the App Store.
Does my subscription include family sharing?
Yes. One $6.99 per month subscription can be shared between up to six people (including you).
How do I cancel Apple Arcade?
First off, keep in mind that if you cancel Apple Arcade (either before your free trial is up or after subscribing), you won’t be able to keep playing the games unless you re-subscribe. If you’re okay with that, you can use the same process you use to cancel any other subscription service. Here’s the easiest way to do it on the iPhone and iPad: 
Open the App Store app and tap on your profile photo in the upper right. 
In the screen that pops up, press Subscriptions near the top of the page. 
You’ll then see a list of active subscriptions, and Apple Arcade should be listed there. Tap it. 
You’ll either see Cancel Free Trial or Cancel Subscription toward the middle of the page that appears. Tap whatever option is available, then Confirm Cancellation.
And here’s how to cancel Apple Arcade on the Mac:
Open the App Store app and then press the icon with your profile photo in the lower left. 
The Account window will appear, and you should then click View Information at the top of the window. Enter your password when/if prompted.
When your Account Information appears, scroll down to the Manage section and click the Manage link to the right of Subscriptions. 
When the list of your active subscriptions appears, click Edit to the right of Apple Arcade. 
Toward the middle of the page that appears, you’ll see a button that says either Cancel Free Trial or Cancel Subscription. Click it, then click Confirm Cancellation and Confirm.
Do Apple Arcade games have in-app purchases?
No. In Apple’s words, “since every game includes access to the full experience, including all game features, content, and future updates, no additional purchases will be required.” Even games that have in-app purchases on the App Store won’t have any in Apple Arcade.
Do Apple Arcade games have ads?
Also no. On a related note, Apple says Apple Arcade has no ad tracking.
Is Apple Arcade a game streaming service like GeForce NOW or Xbox Game Streaming?
No. All Apple Arcade games are downloaded.
Are there demos for Apple Arcade games?
No, and they’re not really necessary. Like regular App Store apps, games download quickly and can easily be removed if you don’t want to keep it anymore.
Apple partly envisions Apple Arcade as a way of letting players try out games with more freedom than the App Store currently allows (which is basically none). In Apple’s words, “rather than pay upfront for each game, a subscription to Apple Arcade will give players the opportunity to try any game in the service without risk.” 
The service has a free trial, though, as we’ve seen with other Apple subscription services.
Am I able to keep playing Apple Arcade games if I cancel my subscription?
No. As with most subscription services, you only have access while you’re a subscriber.
Can I use controllers with Apple Arcade games?
Yes. In additional to traditional MFi (Made for iOS) controllers, you can pair some specific Bluetooth controllers for either PlayStation or Xbox with your iPhone, iPad, or Apple TV. Since many Apple Arcade games are playable on Mac and Apple TV (where controller support is more common), many games will support them. Some games, especially those that are also available in the broader App Store and only for iPhone or iPad, have no controller support.
How often are new games released?
Games are typically released on the first Friday of each month. There are some rare exceptions.
What games have been released so far?
There are over 200 games available for Apple Arcade, and the list grows all the time.

title: If we trust it, Home Hub privacy could lead a smart home revolution
content:
A new Apple Home hub could kill "smart" appliances, but only if Apple can succeed in convincing us its devices don't retain audio and video recordings.


Apple's 'not a camera' in-home sensor could mean interesting changes for the smart home
There is a rumor of an Apple-made accessory that resembles a large tube of chapstick that could accompany Apple's rumored Home hub tablet. It would have a sensor in it that captures footage at a low frame rate, but doesn't actually "record" video.
I discussed this on the AppleInsider Podcast as an interesting concept. Instead of needing a computer chip in every component of our home, Apple could use such sensors to "understand" statuses around the home.

title: Microsoft really wants my old MacBook
content:
Macworld





Did you see that the new Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra has a magnetic USB-C port? Yeah, yeah, I know, MacBooks have MagSafe, blah blah, blah. But magnetic USB-C! That’s so cool. How cool? So cool that I’m considering switching from this M5 Max MacBook Pro that I’m typing on now!
Wait, it gets better. Now that I’m going to switch over to glorious magnetic USB-C, Microsoft wants to make it easier by taking my MacBook in a trade-in. Wow, bold move, Microsoft. It feels like when I traded in my old gas car for my sparkling electric vehicle–I’m leaving behind the old and entering a new frontier. Crazy. I mean, Apple only takes old Macs on trade-ins. Microsoft taking MacBook trade-ins? Lil’ Finder Guy is spinning on his head, wherever he is. (Y’all notice Guy hasn’t been around lately? I digress.)
Going through Microsoft’s value finder on its Surface Laptop Ultra website, they’re offering $2,115 for the M5 Max MacBook Pro (128GB RAM, 4TB SSD) that’s on my lap right now. It was worth $6,149 when new. I guess that’s the price to pay for magnetic USB-C!
I also checked to see what I could get for an old 12-inch base model MacBook–remember that laptop? The one with a single USB-C port that’s not even magnetic? Microsoft’s AI behind the value generator probably laughed when it created its offer of $32.37.
But seriously, Microsoft is making a push for MacBook Pro users. Head over to the Surface Laptop Ultra site and you’ll see that Microsoft is advertising up to $1,000 when you trade in an eligible MacBook Pro and buy one of its new laptops, specifically telling buyers to “break up” with Apple:
Break up with your MacBook
If you’ve outgrown the compromises of a traditional professional laptop, we’ll help make the switch. Level up to Surface Laptop Ultra and get up to $1,000 cash back when you trade in an eligible MacBook Pro.12 We’re confident that once today’s creators and developers experience everything Surface Laptop Ultra has to offer, they won’t look back. Learn more about the offer here.

				
					

				
			
Microsoft




Low trade-in values are nothing new. Apple’s values are on the low side, too. It reminds me of when I traded in my old gas car for my EV (did I mention that it sparkled?). Also, as my PCWorld colleague Mark Hachman points out, Microsoft is mum about the Surface Ultra Laptop’s battery life and power draw. I mean, that’s about as red a red flag can get. 
So yeah, I don’t think I want magnetic USB-C that badly. After all, MacBooks have MagSafe. Good enough for me.

title: Bose’s flagship noise cancelling headphones are $400 less than AirPods Max today
content:
Macworld





		
Bose QuietComfort
View Deal
No matter if it’s your neighbor’s dogs that bark when you’re trying to concentrate on reading, the other commuters talking too loudly, or your coworkers yapping about the game last night, a good pair of noise-cancelling headphones can block everything out for you. If AirPods Max are too expensive for your budget—and we don’t blame you—there are plenty of equally good alternatives out there for much less. For example, the Bose QuietComfort headphones are down to $169 right now, from their usual $359. That’s $190 off, more than 50 percent, and the lowest price ever.
Like AirPods Max, the Bose headphones are great at canceling the world around you, so traffic and chatter won’t distract you. title: Those iPhone 18 Pro production cuts are actually a really good sign
content:
Macworld





Apple’s stock took a bit of a tumble today following a report from Nikkei Asia that iPhone 18 Pro orders have been cut by as much as 20 percent due to “soft demand.” The publication cites the new phones’ prices as the main reason for the pullback, with Apple raising starting prices by $100 on the back on soaring memory and storage costs.
Of course, we’ve heard all this before. Every year, overseas outlets run stories about iPhone production cuts as Apple shifts orders to accommodate customer demand. Apple’s stock ebbs and flows on the news, and it generally ends up being much ado about nothing once Apple releases its quarterly earnings.
This year’s report holds considerably more weight due to the current market conditions, and there’s probably some truth to the notion that some people are holding off on buying a new phone. The iPhone 18 Pro isn’t a huge upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro, the cheaper models don’t arrive until next year, and higher storage models are much more expensive than they have ever been. It all adds up to the likelihood that Apple is probably selling fewer iPhone Pro models than it did last year.
But there’s another possibility. In just a week, Apple will open preorders for the iPhone Duo, its first folding phone, which starts at $1,999. It’s the most expensive phone Apple has ever sold and is expected to sell out very quickly due to supply constraints, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see some models backordered through 2027 within hours of availability. So it would make sense that Apple is shifting 15-20 percent of production to its higher-margin, very popular new model.
If you look at the spec sheet, you’ll see that the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo share the same processor/memory and storage capacities, which happen to be the biggest reason for supply issues. So again, it would make sense for Apple to cut production for the iPhone 18 Pro to free up those components for the iPhone Duo.
Want more evidence that this isn’t a sign of doom and gloom? Back in 2017, it was reported on October 19 that Apple had cut production of the iPhone 8 by a whopping 50 percent due to what one carrier called “anemic” sales. That phone started at $699, while the iPhone X, which would go on sale a week later, started at $999, the first iPhone to break the thousand-dollar barrier. Sound familiar?
We reported late last month that Apple had already set up a pre-preorder page for the iPhone Duo that does little more than let you choose a color and storage size. It’s not about convenience or ease of ordering—Apple uses systems like these to gauge interest and demand for its devices, and something tells me that it’s going to be “blown away” by the demand for the iPhone Duo. So don’t worry, Apple is doing just fine.

title: Leak Details iPhone Features for Apple's LG Home Accessories
content:
Smart home accessories that Apple reportedly helped LG develop could offer iPhone proximity controls and a way to begin setup before the devices have power, according to findings shared by the leaker known as "pdfu."


The findings concern the upcoming LG-branded accessory range that Bloomberg revealed earlier this week. The lineup reportedly includes a thermostat, temperature sensor, deadbolt lock, wired video doorbell, and several security cameras. Apple apparently co-developed the accessories.

Dynamic Island will present an "Open Controls" option for products such as thermostats. Cameras and doorbells will instead display a camera viewer.

The interaction will also apparently work on iPads and iPhones without a ‌Dynamic Island‌, using a notification that remains visible for 30 seconds. A setting in the Home app will let users switch proximity controls off after configuring the accessory.

MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris identified the Dynamic Island references earlier this week. Pdfu says the underlying feature has appeared in code since iOS 27.0, with its settings changing during development. Earlier versions included an option to open controls automatically, but the enabled setting in iOS 27.2 currently asks users to open them through a prompt.

According to the leaker, the accessories will use an identifier stored on an NFC tag alongside a Bluetooth Low Energy broadcast to support recognition and proximity interactions. Tapping a device for the first time will also produce ‌Dynamic Island‌ feedback as setup begins.


Apple's "second-party" LG accessories will debut another Home feature: Proximity Control.
As with HomePod, tapping or bringing iPhone near the accessory shows a hint in the Dynamic Island. An "Open Controls" button opens the accessory's controls. Cameras and doorbells show a camera viewer.
An iPhone without a Dynamic Island or an iPad will show a 30-second notification instead. You can disable this behavior in the Home app after setup.
You'll also see feedback in the Dynamic Island as iPhone launches setup when you first tap the accessory to pair it.
Behind the scenes, the accessory writes an "apple-deviceid" in the Matter payload stored on its NFC tag that helps iOS identify it when tapped. It also broadcasts a Bluetooth Low Energy advert for Apple Proximity Control.
The feature appears in code since iOS 27.0. In earlier versions, Apple showed three presentation options instead of the on/off toggle in iOS 27.2:
•  Never: Suppresses proximity controls.​
•  Ask to Launch: ​Shows Dynamic Island hint or notification, which deep links the control card.
•  Launch Automatically: Shows control card.​
In the current implementation, the enabled state is equivalent to Ask to Launch. Home's helper text reads: "Show controls when you bring your iPhone near your [accessory]." The feature is still in active development across beta releases, so the final behavior may change.

title: Best USB-C and Thunderbolt cables for iPhone, iPad and Mac for 2026
content:
Macworld





USB-C is the modern connection standard shared by most new devices today. It comes in several different formats—USB-C, USB4 and Thunderbolt—but they all have the same reversible connector at the end and are interchangeable and backwards compatible. All of Apple’s new devices now use USB-C or Thunderbolt for charging and data transfers.
Some cables are only really good for charging as their data-transfer (bandwidth) rate is too slow to be practical. In the reviews below we note both charging power (measured in watts) and data-transfer rate—measured in either megabits per second (Mbps) or gigabits per second (Gbps). If you are connecting the cable to a monitor, storage device, hub or docking station the minimum data speed should be 5Gbps but go higher if you can. If you just want to use it for charging an iPhone, iPad or MacBook, the data speed matters less.
We’ve tried and tested the best USB-C and Thunderbolt cables here. If you want to jump straight to our recommendations click the one that meets your requirements:
Best USB-C cable for iPhone and iPad
Best USB-C cable for Mac
Best Thunderbolt 5 cables
Best Thunderbolt 4 cables
You can find cheaper online but we recommend cables only from trusted brands, such as Anker, Apple, Beats, Belkin, Cable Matters, CalDigit, Native Union, Plugable, and Ugreen. When charging your precious devices, you want to be sure that you aren’t putting them at risk of overheating and potentially causing a fire in your home.
Apple’s old Lightning connector was also reversible—where it doesn’t matter which side of the connector faces up or down as you plug it in—so no big change there, but USB-C is much more than just a symmetrical design. It can transfer data much faster—pushing Lightning’s 0.48Gbps to up to 120Gbps.
Apple’s iPhone 15 and newer have a USB-C port, replacing the old trusty but proprietary Lightning cable that has been a part of iPhones and older iPads since 2012. Apple supplies a USB-C charging cable in the box, but if you want a single cable for fast charging and data transfers—or just a spare charging cable—we’ve rounded up some of our favorites to help you get the best one.
Some are fast, some are super-powerful, some are both, a few are retractable, and some are just fun. Yes… fun!
We go into more detail about everything you need to know about USB-C cables after the chart of best cables, but for now you need to know about the cable of your dreams:
Which speed (measured in watts) your devices require: an iPhone needs at least 20W to fast-charge, an iPad 30W, a MacBook Air at least 70W, a MacBook Pro 100W and the 16-inch Pro 140W. While the MacBook Neo doesn’t officially support fast charging, a 30W charger will speed things up but any higher won’t likely do much more for that laptop model.
Do you need it to transfer data as well as supply power? Most charging cables are limited to a rather slow 480Mbps data rate. If you want proper bandwidth as well as charging power look for at least 5Gbps or as much as 80Gbps.
How long should it be: if the charger is within arms reach of your device a short cable might suffice where a long cable will just be an inconvenience, but if you want to charge your iPhone, Pad or MacBook while sat on the sofa a longer cable will make all the difference.
We’ve supplied the cable data to these questions in our reviews below.
The difference between USB-A, Lightning, USB-C, and Thunderbolt

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Thunderbolt looks identical to USB-C and uses the same connector, but is much faster. Thunderbolt 3 and 4 can reach 40Gbps, and Thunderbolt 5 stretches as far as 80Gbps (and even 120Gbps unidirectionally).
Note that the cables reviewed here are USB-C to USB-C (or backwards-compatible Thunderbolt to Thunderbolt). Old iPhone chargers had the non-reversible rectangular USB-A connector to connect to the charger and a Lightning connector that went into the iPhone. Don’t stick with legacy USB-A at one end as the old standard is limited in data transfer speed to 10Gbps and pegged back in charging speed to just a rather pathetic 15W.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Using a USB-C charger will enable fast charging even for iPhones with a Lightning port. You can still charge an Apple device with a USB-A charger but not at the fastest speed. From the iPhone 15 onwards it’s USB-C into the charger and USB-C into the iPhone. See our roundup of the best USB-C chargers for iPhone.
We have even more tips that show you the fastest ways to charge an iPhone.
Best USB-C cables for iPhone and iPad
Elsewhere we have rounded up the best Lightning cables we’ve seen for iPhones older than the iPhone 15. USB-A is the larger, non-reversible connector. USB-C is required for iPhone fast charging.
From the iPhone 15 onwards—also from the AirPods Pro 2—you’ll need a cable with USB-C on both ends (USB-C-to-USB-C) to charge an iPhone or iPad unless you charge wirelessly: check out the best MagSafe wireless iPhone chargers.
All iPads on sale today feature a USB-C connector. But even the 10th Gen iPad’s USB-C is still limited to a 480Mbps data speed. The iPad mini has a USB-C port that supports 5Gbps; the iPad Air 10Gbps; and the iPad Pro has a USB4/Thunderbolt port that can zip data along at 40Gbps. Check your iPad’s data transfer rate before choosing a new cable.
For charging only, any of the USB-C cables reviewed below will be fine as 20W should be enough to charge even an iPad. But if you are connecting to other devices or syncing via cable, we recommend cables that support faster data transfers. A 10Gbps USB-C cable, such as the Cable Matters cord below, is an excellent option if you don’t want to spend a bundle on Thunderbolt.

If you want every iPhone accessory you own to be made by Apple, go with Apple’s own USB-C Charge Cable as a spare USB-C iPhone charging cable—at 60W it’s powerful enough to charge even a MacBook Air. At $19 / £19 it’s a fine, if comparatively expensive, solution.
Unlike Apple’s rather feeble plastic USB-C to Lightning cables, this 3.3ft (1m) charging cable has a robust woven design that means it is far less likely to fray or break with frequent winding and tugging. Apple also sells a $29 2m USB-C Charge Cable that is now also woven—it’s rated at up to 240W, overkill for an iPhone but top-end charging for any Apple USB-C device.
Its USB 2.0 data-transfer speed is super slow compared to 5Gbps or faster USB-C cables but it’s the same as Lightning. That doesn’t make a difference when charging your iPhone but if you are syncing an iPad or Mac via cable, transfer speeds will be frustrating. As the iPhone 15/16/17/18 Pro models boast 10Gbps data transfer, this cable’s low bandwidth is a bit of a disappointment if you use the cable for syncing.

Best USB-C cables for Mac
Only the MacBook Neo uses standard USB-C. Other Macs since the 2016 MacBook Pro have much faster Thunderbolt ports: either Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5. Plain M1/M2 Macs (not Pro or Max) are listed as Thunderbolt/USB4 but can be regarded as the same as Thunderbolt 4 except for their one-screen limitation. Some of Apple’s latest Macs feature Thunderbolt 5, which has a potential data transfer rate of 80Gbps (120Gbps for video) and 240W charging power.
If you are buying today, we recommend you go for a Thunderbolt 4 or 5 cable, which are the most capable standards and fully backward compatible with Thunderbolt 3 and USB-C. But they’re pricey, and if speedy data transfer is not a priority or you require the cable for charging only, a slower USB-C cable will suffice for fast charging. Below our list of recommended Mac USB-C cables we list our favorite Thunderbolt cables. 
MacBooks require cables and chargers that support the USB Power Delivery (PD) standard. PD 3.0 supports up to 100W. PD 3.1 goes up to 240W.
Check the maximum charging wattage supported by the cable. Smaller MacBooks require at least 45W, mid-sized 60W, and larger 100W. The 16-inch MacBook Pro can be fast-charged at 140W.

Thunderbolt  cables
Macs use the Thunderbolt standard that is faster and more capable than USB-C. If all you require the cable for is charging, then the relevant USB-C charging cable should be fine, but for anything requiring fast data transfers go for higher-bandwidth Thunderbolt. Thunderbolt cables are all certified to both speedy charging and very fast data-transfer speeds, whereas you need to check that the USB-C cables you think will do the job actually will—although buy from our recommendations above and you should be fine.
Standard copper “passive” Thunderbolt cables are also usually shorter as the data loses speed over longer distances. To get around this requires an “active” Thunderbolt cable that includes sophisticated chip engineering to push the signal along at the best speed, but you’ll see the price increase accordingly. Anything over 1m in length usually requires active technology.
Best Thunderbolt 5 cables
Thunderbolt 5 is superior to Thunderbolt 4 with doubled data/video bandwidth (80/120Gbps vs 40Gbps), improved PCIe 4.0 support (32Gbps vs 64Gbps), and enhanced power delivery (240W vs 100W). It’s backwards compatible all the way back to USB-C so—if you can afford it—it’s a more future-proof solution than Thunderbolt 3 or 4. Thunderbolt 5 transmits up to 80Gbps bidirectionally and 120Gbps in one direction with Bandwidth Boost enabled to support demanding display configurations.
